Rashi on Gittin 35a:10:1.hebrew: וליאדרה - כדתנן: "נודרת ליתומים כל מה שירצו":
Rashi on Gittin 35a:10:1.english: And let him administer a vow to her - as we learned in the Mishnah: "She vows to the orphans whatever they wish":

Rashi on Gittin 35a:10:2.hebrew: קילי נדרי - קלים היו נדרים בעיניהם לעבור עליהם, הלכך לא סמכינן אנדרה לאגבוייה:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:10:2.english: Vows were light - Vows were [considered] light in their eyes [such that they would] transgress them; therefore, we do not rely on her vow to collect [her ketubah] for her:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:11:1.hebrew: בקופצת - הואיל וקפצה ונשבעה, הרי נשבעה וגובה:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:11:1.english: With regard to one who leaps - Since she leaped [forward] and swore, behold, she has sworn and she collects [her marriage contract]:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:13:1.hebrew: אין לה מזונות - מעתה, דגליא דעתה דבעי לאינסובי, ואיהו לא אתני בהדה אלא "כל ימי מיגר ארמלותיך בביתי" — שהיא אלמנה בשביל כבודו:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:13:1.english: She has no [right to] sustenance - from now on, since she has revealed her intention that she wishes to remarry, and he only stipulated with her [in the marriage contract,] "all the days of your dwelling in widowhood in my house" — [meaning] that she remains a widow for his honor:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:14:1.hebrew: כבי תרי דיינת לי - כרב דלא מגבי כתובה, וכשמואל להפסיד מזונות, ע"כ:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:14:1.english: Like two [judges] you have judged for me - Like Rav, who does not [allow her to] collect [her] ketubah, and like Shmuel, [causing her] to forfeit [her] sustenance [up to here]:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:14:2.hebrew: הפכו לכורסי' ותרצוה - הפכו כסאו וזקפוהו, כדי שתתקיים הקללה בכך. פ"א: "הפכו לכורסייה" — תשפל גדולתו:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:14:2.english: They overturned his chair and stood it upright - They overturned his chair and stood it upright, so that the curse would be fulfilled thereby. Another explanation: "Overturn his chair" — may his greatness be brought low:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:14:3.english: He was not saved from weakness - He was not spared from falling into illness:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:15:1.hebrew: אדרה בב"ד - כל מה שירצו יתומים:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:15:1.english: Administer a vow to her in court - [regarding] whatever the orphans wish:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:15:2.hebrew: וליפול באודני - חפץ אני שישמע הקול באזני, שהוגבה כתובה בימי:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:15:2.english: And let it fall into my ears - I wish for the report to be heard in my ears that a marriage contract [ketubah] was collected in my days:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:15:3.hebrew: דבעינן דאיעביד בה מעשה - כשמואל רבי, להוציא מלבן של תלמידיו של רב, כגון רב הונא ובית דינו, שלא היו מגבין כתובות אלמנה:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:15:3.english: For we desire that I perform an action with it - [Acting] in accordance with Shmuel, my teacher, to disabuse Rav's students — such as Rav Huna and his court — who would not allow widows' marriage contracts to be collected:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:16:1.hebrew: אבל גרושה משביעין - דלא טרחא קמייהו, ולא מוריא היתירא:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:16:1.english: However, [with regard to] a divorcée, [the court] administers an oath [to her] - For she does not toil for them [the orphans], and [therefore] she does not rationalize [taking property as] permitted:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:17:1.english: And a divorcée - Is a vow not sufficient for her? [This is asked] as a question:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:17:2.hebrew: והא שלחו מתם - האשה מבבל היתה, והלכה היא ובעלה לארץ ישראל, וגרשה שם, ותבעתו כתובתה, ועשו לה פסק דין על נכסיו שבבבל:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:17:2.english: But didn't they send from there - The woman was from Babylonia, and she and her husband went to the Land of Israel, and he divorced her there, and she claimed her marriage contract [payment] from him, and [the court] issued a ruling for her against his property in Babylonia:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:17:3.english: Who is called Ayya Mari - Such was his nickname:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:17:4.english: And she vows and prohibits all produce in the world upon herself - if she received [anything else] from her marriage contract:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:17:6.english: And Proverbs [umimshalot] - [This refers to] the Book of Proverbs:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:1:1.english: Due to favor - So that men will find favor in the eyes of women to marry them:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:3:1.english: May [poison] benefit - [It] will avail to kill him:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:4:1.hebrew: דאשתרשי לה מקום דינר - נשתכרה בו עיסה כעובי הדינר, שאם לא היה הדינר היתה נותנת עוד עיסה בככר:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:4:1.english: Because she benefited from the place of the dinar - she gained dough through it [equal to] the thickness of the dinar, for if the dinar were not [there], she would have put more dough into the loaf:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:5:1.english: And what [is meant by] "one who takes an oath truthfully"? - This [oath] is not true:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:5:2.hebrew: כמי שנשבע באמת - דהא שוגגת היא, ומפני שעונש שבועה מרובה נמנעו מלהשביעה:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:5:2.english: Like one who takes an oath truthfully - For she acted inadvertently, and because the punishment for [a false] oath is great, they refrained from administering an oath to her:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:7:1.hebrew: אתיא לאורויי היתירא - בדבר מועט, וסבורה שאין פרעון לה, שבשכר טורחה נוטלתו:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:7:1.english: She will come to rule [it] permissible - regarding a small amount, thinking that it is not a payment [of her marriage contract] for her, since she is taking it in compensation for her efforts:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:8:1.hebrew: חוץ לב"ד משביעין אותה - ששבועת הדיינין של תורה היא, ונקט ס"ת בידיה או תפילין, ומשביע לה בשם או בכינוי, כדאשכחן באברהם: "שים נא ידך וגו' ואשביעך בה'" (בראשית כד), ועונשה מרובה; וחוץ לב"ד שבועה דרבנן, בקללת ארור, ולא נקיט מידי, ואין עונשה כל כך:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:8:1.english: Outside of court, they administer an oath to her - Because the oath of the judges [administered in court] is biblical, and one holds a Torah scroll in his hand or tefillin, and [the judge] administers the oath to her with [God's] Name or with a substitute title, as we find with Abraham: "Please put your hand, etc., and I will make you swear by the Lord" (Genesis 24), and its punishment is severe; whereas outside of court, [it is] a rabbinic oath, with a curse of "cursed [be...]," and one does not hold anything [sacred], and its punishment is not as great:

Rashi on Gittin 35a:8:2.hebrew: לא מגבי כתובה - משום דנמנעו מלהשביעה, ואם איתא, לישבעה חוץ לבית דין ולגבייה כתובתה:
Rashi on Gittin 35a:8:2.english: Does not collect [payment of] a marriage contract - Because they refrained from administering an oath to her; and if it is so [that an oath may be administered outside of court], let him administer an oath to her outside of court and let her collect her marriage contract:

Tosafot on Gittin 35a:17:1.hebrew: ונודרת ואוסרת פירות שבעולם עליה שלא קיבלה מכתובתה כו' - ל"ג "כל פירות", דאע"ג דנדר חייל אף על דבר שאינו יכול לקיים, כדאמר בפרק שני דנדרים (דף טו.) גבי "קונם עיני בשינה", דפריך: ואי לא יהיב שיעורא למילתיה, מי שבקינן ליה עד דעבר באיסור "בל יחל"? והא"ר יוחנן: שבועה שלא אישן ג' ימים — מכין אותו וישן לאלתר! והא דנדרי הבאי מותרים, כדאמר בפרק ג' דנדרים (דף כד:), לאו משום דאסר עצמו במה שאינו יכול לקיים, כגון דאמר: יאסרו כל הפירות שבעולם עלי אם לא ראיתי גמל פורח באויר ונחש כקורת בית הבד; אלא לפי שאין דעתו לומר ממש גמל, ולא ממש כקורת בית הבד, אלא מה שהוא טרוף בגבו מאד ומשונה משאר נחשים, קורא "כקורת בית הבד", וחיל גדול מאד שראה, קורא "כעולי מצרים", ואינו אומר כן אלא להחזיק דבריו. ודוקא שבועות הבאי אסור מדרבנן, דהחמירו משום דכתיב בה "לא ינקה"; אבל נדרי הבאי — ואפילו לא אמר "כל הפירות", אלא אסר עליה חד פירא — שרי בנדר, ואין חילוק בין "כל פירות" ובין "חד פירא". מ"מ הכא ל"ג "כל פירות", דאע"פ שעוברת לאלתר ב"בל יחל" אם קבלה מכתובתה, כיון דמשם ואילך לא מיתסרא — כדאמר: מכין אותו וישן לאלתר — אינה חוששת, הואיל ואינה עומדת באיסור כל ימיה, כדמפרש בסמוך. וא"ת: בפ' בתרא דנדרים (דף פט:), דאמר ההוא גברא דאמר "תיתסר הנאות דעלמא עלי אי נסיבנא איתתא עד דלא תנינא הלכתא כו'", ואתא רב אחא ושבשיה ואנסביה איתתא ושרקיה טינא כדי שלא יהנה מן העולם — מה מועיל מאי דשרקיה? דכי אנסביה מיד עבר, כיון שאין יכול בסוף לקיים! וי"ל: דדוקא בשעה שנודר, אם אי אפשר לו לקיים, עובר לאלתר; אבל התם, בשעה שנדר היה יכול לקיים, דאפשר לו שלא ישא; אע"ג דכי אנסביה אין יכול לקיים, אינו עובר לאלתר עד שיהנה:
Tosafot on Gittin 35a:17:1.english: And she takes a vow and prohibits the produce of the world to herself, that she did not receive from her marriage contract, etc. - We do not have the reading "all produce"; for even though a vow takes effect even on something that one cannot fulfill — as [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Nedarim (15a) regarding [one who says], "Sleep is konam [forbidden] to my eyes," where [the Gemara] asks: If he did not set a limit to his statement, do we leave him until he transgresses the prohibition of "he shall not profane [his word]"? Did not Rabbi Yoḥanan say: [If one takes] an oath that "I will not sleep for three days," they flog him and he may sleep immediately! And [as for] that which [the Mishnah states, that] vows of exaggeration are permitted, as [the Gemara] says in the third chapter of Nedarim (24b), [that is] not because he prohibited himself with something that he cannot fulfill — such as where he said, "May all the produce in the world be forbidden to me if I did not see a camel flying in the air" or "a snake like the beam of an olive press" — rather, [it is] because his intention is not to say literally a [flying] camel, nor literally [a snake as large as] the beam of an olive press; rather, [a snake] that is heavily spotted on its back and unusual compared to other snakes, he calls "like the beam of an olive press," and a very large army that he saw, he calls "like those who went up from Egypt," and he only speaks thus in order to reinforce his words. And specifically oaths of exaggeration are forbidden by rabbinic decree, for [the Sages] were stringent [with oaths] because it is written regarding [an oath], "He will not hold guiltless"; but [with] vows of exaggeration — even if he did not say "all produce," but rather prohibited to himself a single fruit — it is permitted in the case of a vow, and there is no difference between "all produce" and "a single fruit." Nevertheless, here we do not have the reading "all produce," for even though she immediately transgresses "he shall not profane [his word]" if she [already] received from her marriage contract, since from then onward she is not prohibited — as [the Gemara] says, "they flog him and he may sleep immediately" — she is not concerned, since she does not remain in a state of prohibition all her days, as [the Gemara] explains immediately below. And if you ask: In the last chapter of Nedarim (89b), where [the Gemara] relates [that] a certain man said, "May all pleasures of the world be forbidden to me if I marry a woman before I have studied the halakhot, etc.," and Rav Aḥa came and tricked him and married him to a woman, and smeared him with mud so that he would not derive pleasure from the world — what does smearing him [with mud] avail? For as soon as he married him [off], he immediately transgressed, since he cannot ultimately fulfill [the vow]! And one can answer: Specifically at the time he vows, if it is impossible for him to fulfill [it], he transgresses immediately; but there, at the time he vowed he was able to fulfill [it], since it was possible for him not to marry; [therefore,] even though when he married him [off] he could not fulfill [it], he does not transgress immediately until he derives pleasure:

Tosafot on Gittin 35a:3:1.hebrew: לא היו ימים מועטים - וא"ת, ומאי טעמא איענש? הא אמרינן בפ"ג דשבועות (דף כו.): "האדם בשבועה" — פרט לאנוס, כדרב כהנא ורב אסי, דמר משתבע "הכי אמר רב" ומר משתבע "הכי אמר רב", וכי אתו לקמיה דרב ואמר כחד מינייהו, אמר ליה אידך: ואנא בשקרא אישתבעי! ואמר ליה: את לבך אנסך. וליכא למימר דלא ממעט קרא התם אלא למפטר מקרבן, אבל עונש איכא, כדאשכחן בפ"ב דנדרים (דף יז.) גבי נשבע לבטל את המצוה, דמיבעי לן תרי קראי, חד למיפטריה מקרבן וחד למיפטריה מלאו [והכא דליכא אלא חד קרא למיפטריה מקרבן], אבל עונש דשבועת שוא איכא — דהא "לבך אנסך" משמע: ולא נשבעת לשקר! ועוד, דבפ"ג דנדרים (דף כה:) מייתי דרב כהנא ורב אסי אשבועות שגגות, דתניא בגמרא: כשם שנדרי שגגות מותרות, כך שבועות שגגות מותרות; ומפ' שבועות שגגות כדרב כהנא ורב אסי, דמשמע דמותרות ואפי' עונש ליכא. ולא דמי לנשבע לבטל את המצוה דאיכא עונש שבועת שוא, דהתם מיבעי לן ב' קראי, אחד למיפטר שוגג מקרבן ואחד למיפטר מזיד ממלקות; וכשפטר שוגג לגמרי, פטרו מעונש ומקרבן, וה"ה גבי "האדם בשבועה" — פרט לאנוס, דפטור לגמרי. וי"ל דהכא גבי פקדון הוה לה להזהר יותר לשמרו היטב, והוה לה לאסוקי אדעתא שתבא לידי שבועה:
Tosafot on Gittin 35a:3:1.english: Not a few days - And if you will ask: Why was [she] punished? Behold, we say in the third chapter of Shevuot (26a): "[That] a person [utters] with an oath" — excluding one who is compelled [by circumstances], as in [the incident of] Rav Kahana and Rav Assi, where one swore, "Thus said Rav," and the other swore, "Thus said Rav," and when they came before Rav and he ruled like one of them, the other said to him, "Then I swore falsely!" and [Rav] said to him, "Your heart compelled you." And one cannot say that the verse there only excludes [him] from being liable for a sacrifice, but there is [still] punishment — just as we find in the second chapter of Nedarim (17a) regarding one who swears to nullify a mitzvah, where we need two verses, one to exempt him from a sacrifice and one to exempt him from a negative prohibition [and here, where there is only one verse to exempt him from a sacrifice], yet there is the punishment of a vain oath — for "your heart compelled you" implies: and you did not swear falsely! And furthermore, in the third chapter of Nedarim (25b), [the Gemara] cites [the incident of] Rav Kahana and Rav Assi regarding unwitting oaths, as it is taught in the Gemara: Just as unwitting vows are permitted, so too unwitting oaths are permitted; and [the Gemara] explains "unwitting oaths" as [referring to the incident of] Rav Kahana and Rav Assi, which implies that they are permitted and there is not even punishment. And it is not comparable to one who swears to nullify a mitzvah, where there is the punishment of a vain oath, for there we need two verses — one to exempt an unwitting [transgressor] from a sacrifice and one to exempt an intentional [transgressor] from lashes; and when [Scripture] exempted an unwitting [transgressor] completely, it exempted him from [both] punishment and a sacrifice, and the same applies to "[that] a person [utters] with an oath" — excluding one who is compelled, that he is completely exempt. And one can answer that here, regarding a deposit, she should have been more careful to guard it well, and she should have brought it to mind that she might come to [take] an oath:

Tosafot on Gittin 35a:7:1.hebrew: דמוריא היתרא - ולכך נמנעו מלהשביעה, שעונש שבועה מרובה, אלא בהדרה, דלא חמיר כולי האי. והשתא בזמן הזה תקנו לקבל חרם במקום שבועה, שלא יהא העונש גדול כל כך:
Tosafot on Gittin 35a:7:1.english: That she rationalizes and permits [it] - And therefore they refrained from administering an oath to her, because the punishment for [a false] oath is great; rather, [they did so] through a vow, which is not so severe. And now, in this time, they instituted accepting a ban (cherem) in place of an oath, so that the punishment will not be so great:

Tosafot on Gittin 35a:8:1.hebrew: לא שנו אלא בב"ד - פי' בקונטרס דחמירא, משום דהויא באנקוטי חפצא ואיכא עונש טפי. והא דאמר בהכותב (כתובות דף פח.): "אי פקח הוא מייתי לה לידי שבועה דאורייתא" — לא כמו שפי' בקונט' (שם) דנפקא מינה בין דאורייתא לדרבנן לענין אנקוטי חפצא, דאפי' שבועה דרבנן הויא באנקוטי חפצא, כדפי' הקונט' בעצמו כאן; אלא יש לחלק בין דאורייתא לדרבנן, כמו שמפרש בערוך, דשבועה דאורייתא הויא בכבוי נרות. ועוד, בריש שבועת הדיינים (שבועות דף מא.) מפרש חילוק בין דאורייתא לדרבנן (ובההיא פירקא מפרש מאי איכא בין שבועה דאורייתא לדרבנן, והתם לא מידכר חילוק דכבוי ולאנקוטי חפצא):
Tosafot on Gittin 35a:8:1.english: They taught only in court - Rashi explained that [an oath in court] is stringent because it is [administered] while holding a [sacred] object, and there is greater punishment [for swearing falsely]. And that which [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] HaKotev (Ketubot 88a), "If he is clever, he brings her to a biblical oath" — [this is] not as Rashi explained (there), that the practical difference between a biblical [oath] and a rabbinic [oath] is with respect to holding a [sacred] object; for even a rabbinic oath is [administered] while holding a [sacred] object, as Rashi himself explained here; rather, one must distinguish between a biblical [oath] and a rabbinic [oath] as the Arukh explains, that a biblical oath is [administered] with the extinguishing of candles. Furthermore, at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Shevuat HaDayanim (Shevuot 41a), [the Gemara] explains the difference between a biblical [oath] and a rabbinic [oath] (and in that chapter it explains what [difference] there is between a biblical oath and a rabbinic [oath], and there no distinction of extinguishing [candles] or of holding a [sacred] object is mentioned):
